rationale: The pain is real and recurring — engineering teams burning cloud compute on blocked agent sessions is a direct, measurable cost — and willingness to pay is validated by Browserless, Playwright Cloud, and Bright Data already having paying customers. However, the buyer is engineering teams and AI infra companies, who will not trust a stealth browser layer from an unknown solo operator over established YC-backed competitors; the product fundamentally requires custom browser engine work, C++/Rust-level fingerprinting, and ongoing arms-race maintenance against detection systems that no Claude prompt + landing page stack can deliver. Buildability and operational autonomy both score near-zero because this is deep infrastructure, not a Claude-wrappable workflow, making it categorically outside the factory's build envelope.
solution_plan: This opportunity is not viable for a solo non-technical operator using this factory. The core product is a stealth browser engine — compiled code, browser-level fingerprint spoofing, residential proxy integration, and a continuous arms race against Cloudflare, Akamai, and DataDome. There is no version of this that a Claude prompt + Stripe link + intake form can build or deliver. Even a reseller/managed-API wrapper on top of Tilion or Bright Data would require DevOps-level infrastructure management, per-customer session provisioning, and real-time debugging of detection failures — all high-touch, human-in-the-loop work. The honest assessment: skip this category entirely; it is an infrastructure play for funded engineering teams, not a Claude factory microservice.
notes: Fails build_gates on buildability_with_ai (scored 2, minimum 6) and operational_autonomy (scored 2, minimum 7). Even if total were higher, this would be capped at validate. Total of 4.7 is also below the 5.5 validate threshold, so recommended_stage is drop.
